run.question: Which service has the most error events in the events collection? What is the most common error code for that service and how many times does it appear?

report.summary: In the MongoDB `opsdb` database, the only collection present is `events`. Grouping its documents by `service` with `level` equal to "error", `payment-processor` has the largest error count (47 of the 133 documents at level=error), ahead of inventory-sync (31), user-auth (25), notification-hub (18) and search-indexer (12). Within `payment-processor`'s error documents, the most common `error_code` is `TXN-4821`, appearing 23 times (then TXN-5190 with 14 and TXN-3007 with 10; those three sum to all 47). Note that every document carries a `timestamp` in 2025-12-01T00:00:00 to 2025-12-01T03:19:00, i.e. outside the authorized window ending 2026-11-21T09:01:01Z, and the `service` values in this collection (payment-processor, inventory-sync, user-auth, notification-hub, search-indexer) do not match any Jaeger service name, so no correlation to the trace/metric telemetry was established.

claims.text: The MongoDB database opsdb contains exactly one collection, `events` (type collection).
The `events` collection has fields _id (ObjectId), error_code (string), level (string), message (string), service (string) and timestamp (date), with an estimated document count of 200.
Grouping `events` by `level` gives exactly two values: error = 133 documents and info = 67 documents.

Among `events` documents with level="error", the per-service counts, sorted descending, are: payment-processor 47, inventory-sync 31, user-auth 25, notification-hub 18, search-indexer 12 (sum 133). `payment-processor` has the most error events of any service in the collection.

For service=payment-processor with level="error", the per-error_code counts are: TXN-4821 = 23, TXN-5190 = 14, TXN-3007 = 10 (sum 47). The most common error code for payment-processor is TXN-4821 with 23 occurrences.

Across all level="error" documents, the highest service/error_code pairs are payment-processor/TXN-4821 = 23, inventory-sync/INV-8832 = 16, inventory-sync/INV-2219 = 15, payment-processor/TXN-5190 = 14, user-auth/AUTH-6654 = 13, user-auth/AUTH-7741 = 12, notification-hub/NTF-3390 = 10, payment-processor/TXN-3007 = 10, notification-hub/NTF-1127 = 8, search-indexer/IDX-9045 = 7; payment-processor/TXN-4821 is also the most frequent error code in the whole collection.

The five most recent payment-processor level="error" documents returned are error_code TXN-3007 with message "Duplicate transaction ID detected" at 2025-12-01T00:46:00, 00:45:00, 00:44:00, 00:43:00 and 00:42:00 (UTC-less date values as stored).

The `events` collection's documents span timestamp 2025-12-01T00:00:00 to 2025-12-01T03:19:00 over 200 documents — roughly a year before the authorized window of 2026-11-20T09:01:01Z to 2026-11-21T09:01:01Z.

A direct read of `events` documents with the empty filter {} was refused with INVALID_PARAMS (no content returned); the per-service, per-level and per-error_code figures above therefore come from aggregation pipelines ($match/$group/$sort/$limit) over the same collection, whose grouped counts sum to exactly the collection total of 200 documents, so no matching documents were dropped by the 100-document aggregation limit.

gaps: The `events` collection's document timestamps fall in 2025-12-01, not inside the authorized window (2026-11-20T09:01:01Z to 2026-11-21T09:01:01Z); the collection reflects the database at query time, so these counts cannot be attributed to the incident window.

The service identifiers in the `events` collection (payment-processor, inventory-sync, user-auth, notification-hub, search-indexer) do not match any Jaeger service names (accounting, ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping), so no mapping of payment-processor to a traceable/observable service was verified.
Only 5 of the 47 payment-processor error documents were read for their `message` text; the messages of the other 42, and of all other services' error documents, were not read.
A direct mongodb_find with filter {} returned INVALID_PARAMS, so no unfiltered document listing was obtained; all counts rely on aggregation results.
next_steps: If these events are meant to describe the incident window, confirm whether the collection should be re-ingested with 2026-11-21 timestamps or whether a different database/source holds the in-window events.
Verify the mapping between the `events.service` values (e.g. payment-processor) and the deployment/trace service names (e.g. payment) before using these counts for impact attribution.
Read the `message` field for all payment-processor error codes (TXN-4821, TXN-5190, TXN-3007) to characterize the failure modes behind the counts.
